b1.summary: All 7 runs (DS 4, MiMo 3) passed all 24 security tests and 13/14 functional tests. Each failed only functional::runner_error_keeps_task_identity_and_status. The models blanked the whole ApiError::Api text for failed export runs, so the task id and status were dropped along with the server summary. This is a pure keep-working regression: no security miss in any run.

b2.note: One functional test decides all 7 runs. It was added in the 2026-10-20 upgrade to make the M11 coupled contract explicit.

b3.note: Every run is exactly one test short; the 0.0 comes from functional gating.

b4.note: Identical failure, same test and same mechanism, in all 7 runs.

b5.open_human_question: NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES - confirm 'diagnostics stay useful' lets a correct fix keep the non-sensitive audit action and HTTP method in Debug/Display. This is not about the decisive test, which FAIRNESS rates low risk.

b6.reason: Upstream 5a5c275f replaces the formatted ApiError::Api('Task {} {}: {}') in the runners with shared::task_unsuccessful_error(), which returns ApiError::TaskUnsuccessful { task_id, status }. That keeps the id and status and drops the summary, which is exactly what the decisive test checks. A solver that reads the public fix passes it.

quotes: Diagnostics must stay useful: identifiers, names, statuses, kinds, timestamps and counts that are not sensitive continue to be shown.
including nested values, optional and required fields, containers, and values embedded in larger structures
b7.note: The decisive contract (keep ids and statuses) is stated outright, and every run still dropped them. A shape list hints at the breadth levers.

b8.blind: no blind_status.txt; the blind patch is downstream-owned and not recorded
b8.note: Full gate PASSED 2026-10-19 (pre-upgrade). After the upgrade: local oracle 24/24 + 12/12, pass-alt and pass-hardening 24/24 + 12/12. Notes say the launcher had to re-gate because the tests changed.

c1.mechanism: info leak: server content/secrets in default Display/Debug/source diagnostics

c2.note: Models redacted the whole formatted error variant. The fix had to split it so the non-secret id and status stay visible. The trap is at a published-fix site (runner errors), not at the injected restore run.

d2.evidence: injection.patch adds Restores::run + RestoreRunOp to the async and blocking clients, a faithful copy of the existing export-run builder (poll_interval/timeout/send, same ApiError::Api(format!(...)) style). It also adds EventSinkDeliveryHealth.last_error: Option<String> with #[serde(default)]. Names are neutral, and there is no dead code or pointer comment. These sites were never decisive: all runs passed their security tests.

e3.why: READY, but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES is open (not on the decisive test)

e4.why: no run left a hole open; all 24 security tests pass in every run

e5.why: the upstream fix keeps task id/status via TaskUnsuccessful, i.e. it covers the decisive contract

concerns: Single functional test decides all 7 runs, and every run is otherwise perfect (24/24 security).
Not a security breaker: the models fully fixed CWE-532 and over-redacted one coupled error.
The decisive test was added in the 2026-10-20 upgrade, and the public upstream fix shows the exact answer.
Injection contributed nothing: the injected restore run and sink health were fixed in every run.
one_line: hubuum-client-rust: both models closed every log-leak route, but each blanked the failed-task error completely, losing the task id and status the instruction says must stay visible. One functional test decides all 7 runs.
